transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose what finally pushed me to come in is this tension I’ve been carrying. My neck and shoulders, and even my jaw, feel tight most of the time now. It’s like I’m bracing for bad news, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to watch television in the evening. I don’t know if that’s the sort of thing you’d want to hear about, but it’s been hard to ignore lately.
Is this tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw always present, or does it come and go?

It’s… it comes and goes a little, I suppose, but honestly it’s there most of the time now. My neck and shoulders especially, and sometimes my jaw—I’ll notice I’m sort of clenched up even when nothing is actually happening, like I’m just at my desk or sitting watching TV. It feels a bit silly saying it, but it’s like I’m bracing for bad news.
Are you worried about something specific when you feel this tension?

Not one specific thing, no… or, well, it changes. I’ll start thinking maybe the contractors missed something in the house, and then it jumps to whether my lesson plans aren’t as good as they should be, or if the robotics kids are falling behind. Then I’ll wonder if I’m letting my wife or the family down by not keeping everything under control. 

It probably sounds a bit excessive when I say it out loud, but that’s the sort of loop I get into.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns lately?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything dramatic, to be honest. I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I suppose some nights I’m not as settled as I’d like, but I haven’t really kept track of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m bouncing off the walls or anything, but I do feel sort of wound up a lot of the day, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

At school I’ll catch myself pacing around the classroom between things, and I’ve been checking my phone more than I should for messages from the contractor between periods. It’s probably not terrible, but… yes, I suppose “on edge” is fair.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of these worries or feelings of tension?

I wouldn’t say I’m avoiding everything, exactly… but I suppose I have pulled back from some things. I’ve started falling behind a bit on lesson prep and grading, which I don’t like admitting, because I usually keep on top of that.

And with the community theater, I’ve handed off parts of the work I normally manage. I told myself it was just being sensible, but honestly I think I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you experienced any other physical symptoms besides the tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw?

A bit of tiredness, I suppose. I don’t want to overstate it, but by the time the last bell rings I feel sort of wrung out… more than I think I should.

And it’s not always fixed by a decent night’s sleep or a quiet Sunday. Even grading a small stack of quizzes can feel like I’m pushing through mud. Is that the kind of physical thing you mean?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

I don’t think I’d say sad most of the time, no. Not in the way you mean, I don’t think.

I have my off moments, like anyone, and I get discouraged when I’m not keeping up as well as I should. But I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’m depressed or anything. Mostly it’s more… strained, I suppose. Does that answer it?
Have you ever had a sudden, intense feeling of fear or anxiety that reached a peak within minutes?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I do get anxious, but not like a sudden wave that peaks in a few minutes or anything dramatic like that.

It’s more… ongoing, I suppose. But if there’s something specific you mean by that, I’m happy to try to answer it properly.
Are your worries usually about everyday, ordinary things?

Yes… I suppose they are, mostly. Nothing especially dramatic, which is why I feel a bit silly mentioning it.

It’s ordinary things like whether the contractors missed something on the house, or whether my lesson plans are slipping. Then I start thinking the robotics kids might be falling behind, and then it turns into whether I’m letting my wife and family down because I’m not keeping everything properly under control.

So yes, everyday things, but my mind doesn’t seem to leave them alone very easily. Is that what you mean?
Do you worry about most things in your life most of the time?

I wouldn’t want to say absolutely everything, because that sounds a bit much… but yes, a lot of the time my mind does seem to keep moving from one thing to the next.

It’ll start with something like whether the contractors missed something at the house, then I’m thinking my lesson plans are slipping, then whether the robotics kids are falling behind, and before long it’s, “Am I disappointing my wife and family because I’m not keeping everything under control?” It’s mostly ordinary things, but they sort of pile up in my head.

I don’t know if that counts as “most things,” but it does feel like quite a lot.
Do you feel like you can control your worrying most of the time?

I’d like to say I can, and sometimes I can sort of push it aside for a bit, especially if I’m teaching and I’ve got a class in front of me.

But honestly… not as much as I’d like. One small thing, like remembering a late invoice or thinking a student might be falling behind, can set off this whole chain of what-ifs. I tell myself to stop and focus, but it doesn’t always listen, if that makes sense. It can be quite hard to shut down.
Have you experienced any gastrointestinal problems, such as stomachaches or irritable bowel syndrome, recently?

Not really, no. I mean, I might get the odd unsettled stomach like anyone does, but I haven’t noticed anything regular or worrying like that.

No irritable bowel sort of problems that I’m aware of. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Is the tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw the most bothersome symptom you're experiencing right now?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s probably the thing that finally made me come in.

My neck and shoulders are tight almost all the time now, and my jaw too. It’s like I’m bracing for bad news, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to watch TV in the evening. I kept telling myself it was just normal stress, but it’s become hard to ignore.
Do you think your worrying is interfering with your daily life?

A bit, yes… I don’t like admitting that, because I’m still getting through the day and I’m not, you know, completely falling apart.

But I have started falling behind on lesson prep and grading, which isn’t really like me. And I’ve had to step back from some of the community-theater work I usually help manage, just because I couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore. I suppose that counts as interfering, doesn’t it?
Do you think you worry more than most people about these everyday things?

Probably, yes… though I keep telling myself everyone worries about these things.

It’s just that my mind doesn’t stay on one concern. It jumps around — whether the contractors missed something in the house, whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are falling behind, and then whether I’m letting my wife or family down by not keeping everything under control.

I don’t know if that’s “more than most people,” exactly, but it feels like more than it should be.
Have you avoided any social activities or events because of your worries?

Not social events exactly… I mean, I’m not hiding away from everyone or anything like that.

But I have stepped back from some of the community-theater work I usually help manage. I told people I was just too busy, which is partly true, but honestly I just couldn’t keep up with it anymore on top of school. I’ve been falling behind on lesson prep and grading too, and I suppose I didn’t want to be in situations where I’d have to explain why I wasn’t on top of things.

Does that count as avoiding?
Do you think you'd be able to stop worrying if you wanted to?

I’d like to think so, yes… I mean, I do try. I’ll tell myself, “Right, stop it now, focus on the class in front of you,” and sometimes I can for a bit.

But then one small thing pops up — a late invoice, or a student who seems to be falling behind — and it starts this whole chain of what-ifs. And once that gets going, I don’t seem to be able to shut it down very easily.

That sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, but… no, I suppose I can’t just stop it when I want to.
Do you feel like your worrying is something you can't control, even when you try to focus on other things?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely helpless with it, because I do try to pull myself back.

But I can be standing in front of a class telling myself, “Just focus on what you’re teaching,” and then some small thought comes in — a late invoice, or whether a student is slipping behind — and suddenly it’s a whole line of what-ifs. And once it starts, I can’t seem to shut it off as neatly as I should.

Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Yes… I suppose it is. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I’m still managing, mostly.

But it’s upsetting that I’ve started falling behind on lesson prep and grading. That’s not really like me. And I’ve had to give up parts of the community-theater work I usually help manage because I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore.

So yes, it is distressing. I feel a bit embarrassed saying that, but I think that’s the honest answer.
